price_position.reading: No price at the cutoff is in the calculator, so where the price sits in the value range cannot be read, and there is no range to place it in. The calculator prints under market.missing: "no price series was given: the forward track's price source is Tiingo, and without its token no series is fetched"; the same reason leaves the beta, the market value of equity and the free-cash-flow yield cross-check empty. No price appears anywhere else in my inputs, and none is supplied or assumed here. What the record does hold is the cash any price would be set against: simple free cash flow of {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_simple} and quality-adjusted free cash flow of {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_quality_adjusted} in fiscal 2026, after negative free cash flow in each earlier filed year, such as {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.1.free_cash_flow_simple} a year earlier. The accounting reader judges the fiscal 2026 cash flattered by customer deposits, advances and unpaid tax, so even with a price, a yield on that figure would overstate recurring cash.

Only the other two sides of the comparison exist. On history, revenue compounded at {implied_growth_beside_history.revenue_growth_three_year_compound|pct} a year across the filed record, measured from a loss-making trough; fiscal 2026 alone grew {ratios.growth.revenue.trailing_four_quarters|pct}, while the two years before it grew {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.1.revenue_growth|pct} and {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.2.revenue_growth|pct}; the five-year compound is not computed because the record holds too few fiscal years. Whether the price at the cutoff assumes growth nearer the trough-to-peak rebound, the guided step or the pre-upturn rates cannot be said until a price and a beta are supplied.

most_sensitive.reading: Python computed no sensitivity grid and no scenario spread, for the reason printed under valuation.missing, so which assumption value is most sensitive to is not measured here. Read from the drivers alone, the year-ten operating margin is one of the two choices that carry the scenarios' disagreement furthest into the future, because it is the margin the terminal year inherits. The bear sets it slightly below the three-year average of {earnings_versus_cash.history.operating_margin_three_year_average|pct}, an average that mixes the fiscal 2026 peak of {ratios.profitability.operating_margin|pct} with losses as deep as {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.3.operating_margin|pct}; the base and the bull set it well above that average and well below the peak. Gross margin was {trend_table.years-back-1.ratios.gross_margin|pct} and {trend_table.years-back-2.ratios.gross_margin|pct} in the two years before the upturn against {ratios.profitability.gross_margin|pct} in fiscal 2026, so the base and bull margins rest on management's view that the new multi-year agreements "reduce certain elements of industry cyclicality", which the filed record has not yet tested through a downturn.

No grid was computed, so this sensitivity is not measured either. Year-one growth is the other choice that carries furthest, because Python fades it in a straight line to the terminal rate at year ten, so the starting rate sets the whole decade's revenue path. All three scenarios start below fiscal 2026 growth of {ratios.growth.revenue.trailing_four_quarters|pct} and the three-year compound of {earnings_versus_cash.history.revenue_growth_three_year_compound|pct}, both measured from loss-making years, and they range from the bear's start close to the pre-upturn rates of {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.1.revenue_growth|pct} and {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.2.revenue_growth|pct} to the bull's start well above them. The recent growth came mostly from price: MD&A reports Consumer volume falling while revenue there rose on pricing, and the release attributes most of the fourth quarter's sequential growth of {ratios.growth.revenue.quarter_over_quarter|pct} to higher pricing, so this driver is also a view on how long price per gigabyte holds.

accounting_adjustments.reading: No DCF value was computed, so how much the accounting adjustments moved value cannot be read; the calculator holds no valuation.accounting_adjustments, only the reason printed under valuation.missing. The accounting reader's two adjustments did reach the calculator's free cash flow: current contract liabilities of {terms.balances_now.contract_liabilities}, customer advances under the new multi-year agreements, and the timing-driven payables increase of {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.accounts_payable.cash_flow_statement_change} each reduce cash flow once, and together with share-based compensation of {terms.trailing_four_quarters.share_based_compensation} they take simple free cash flow of {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_simple} to quality-adjusted free cash flow of {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_quality_adjusted}. Other items the accounting reader named were not applied because they are not in the calculator: refundable customer security deposits, income tax expensed but not yet paid, Flash Ventures distributions moved into operating cash flow, and loans to Flash Forward that fund capacity outside capital expenditure of {terms.trailing_four_quarters.capital_expenditure}. These flatter reported cash rather than the operating margin the DCF drivers start from, so in this reading it is the drivers' reinvestment rates, not an adjustment, that allow for them. The catch-up revenue from re-estimating transaction price, which the accounting reader names and does not apply, would touch the starting margin instead; it is not in the calculator either.
